newsitem.title: USA: Miami cruise ship passengers taken ill.
newsitem.headline: Miami cruise ship passengers taken ill.

text.p: Health officials ordered a cruise ship to remain in port in Florida after more than 350 passengers and crew fell ill during a Caribbean cruise, a newspaper reported on Saturday.

Investigators from the U.S. Centres for Disease Control told Norwegian Caribbean Cruise Line to halt cruises on the vessel Royal Odyssey until they could determine the cause of a sickness that swept the 800-passenger liner this week, the Miami Herald reported.
Officials said 306 of the 781 passengers and 50 of 379 crew experienced vomiting and diarrhoea during the 10-day cruise. The ship left Miami on March 25 and docked at the Port of Miami on Friday.

"Epidemiologists were at the ship Friday morning and early indications point to a viral gastroenteritis," Henry Falk, director of the CDC's Division of Environmental Hazards and Health Effects, told the Herald.
A spokeswoman for the company said the illness appeared to be "some sort of 24 hour virus" and passengers were treated with an over-the counter medication, the newspaper said.
The company said the Royal Odyssey was scheduled to be refurbished, renamed and redeployed in the near future.
